M/s VANASPATI HERBAL PRODUCTS PRIVATE LIMITED

Through its Director Ms. Ritika Surendra Agarwal

CEASE AND DESIST NOTICE
INFRINGEMENT OF REGISTERED TRADE MARK "NANDANVAN" UNDER SECTION 29 OF THE TRADE MARKS ACT, 1999 AND PASSING OFF

Sir / Madam,

I am instructed by and write on behalf of my client, NANDANVAN ORGANICS PRIVATE LIMITED, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at 9th Floor, Sunteck Plaza, Bandra Kurla Complex, Mumbai 400051 (hereinafter "my client"), to give you the following notice.

1. My client is engaged in the business of manufacturing and marketing herbal, ayurvedic and natural skin care, hair care and personal care products since the year 2014, under the trade mark NANDANVAN (word mark and device mark), which is a coined and distinctive mark. My client is the registered proprietor of the trade mark NANDANVAN under Registration No. 2874561 in Class 3 (cosmetics, soaps, hair oils, creams) and Registration No. 2874562 in Class 5 (herbal and ayurvedic preparations), both registered with the Trade Marks Registry, Mumbai, as of 12 March 2015 and valid and subsisting, having been renewed up to 11 March 2035. True copies of the registration certificates are enclosed.

2. My client has used the mark continuously for over twelve (12) years. Its sales under the mark exceeded Rs 46 crore for the Financial Year 2025-26, and it has spent over Rs 5 crore on advertising. The mark has thus acquired substantial goodwill and is associated exclusively with my client.

3. It has recently come to my client's notice that you are using the mark NANDAN VAN HERBALS, together with a leaf device in a green and gold colour scheme, in respect of hair oils, face creams, herbal soaps and herbal shampoos, which are identical to the goods of my client, through your website, various e-commerce marketplaces, retail outlets in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Delhi, and your social media pages. A trade mark application No. 6123987 for the mark NANDAN VAN HERBALS in Class 3 filed by you on 4 June 2025 on a proposed-to-be-used basis is pending, and my client has opposed it under Section 21 of the Act.

4. Your impugned mark is phonetically, visually and structurally identical with or deceptively similar to my client's registered mark NANDANVAN. The mere splitting of the mark into two words, and the addition of the descriptive word "HERBALS", does not distinguish it from my client's mark, and in fact, the same increases the likelihood of confusion, since my client itself markets its products as "herbal" products. The goods are identical, the trade channels and class of customers are identical, and the use is likely to cause confusion and deception among the consuming public, including a likelihood of association with my client.

5. Your said acts constitute infringement of my client's registered trade mark within the meaning of Section 29(1), Section 29(2)(b) and (c), and Section 29(4) of the Trade Marks Act, 1999, as well as passing off at common law, unfair competition and dilution of my client's goodwill. The use of the mark in your trade name and on the internet is also an infringement under Section 29(5) of the Act.

6. You are liable under Section 135 of the Act to injunction, damages or an account of profits, and delivery up of infringing goods. You are also exposed to criminal prosecution under Sections 103 and 104 of the Trade Marks Act, 1999 for applying a false trade mark and selling goods to which a false trade mark is applied, which are cognisable offences punishable with imprisonment of up to three (3) years and fine of up to Rs 2,00,000/-.

7. I, therefore, on behalf of my client, hereby call upon you to do the following within seven (7) days of the date of this notice, that is, on or before 29 October 2026:

(a) immediately cease and desist from using the mark NANDAN VAN HERBALS, NANDANVAN or any other mark or name which is identical or deceptively similar to my client's mark NANDANVAN, in respect of any goods, packaging, advertisements, websites, domain names, social media handles and online marketplace listings;
(b) withdraw all listings of the infringing goods from all e-commerce platforms and take down all infringing content from your website and social media handles;
(c) destroy all the infringing stock, packaging materials, labels, printing blocks, dies and promotional materials in your possession, in the presence of my client's representative, and furnish a certificate of destruction;
(d) withdraw trade mark application No. 6123987 and abandon any claim to the mark;
(e) provide a complete account of sales of the impugned goods since your adoption of the mark, along with the stock position, and pay damages of Rs 7,50,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Fifty Thousand only) to my client; and
(f) furnish a written undertaking, signed by your Director, that you shall not use or apply for registration of any such mark in future.

8. If you fail to comply within the stipulated period of seven (7) days, my client shall, without further notice, initiate civil proceedings before the competent Commercial Court at Mumbai for permanent injunction, damages and delivery up, with an application for ad-interim injunction and appointment of a Local Commissioner, and criminal proceedings, at your risk as to costs.

9. This notice is without prejudice to all the rights of my client, which are reserved. You are advised to preserve all records relating to the impugned mark, as they will be required in litigation.

Yours faithfully,

(Smita A. Deshmukh)
Advocate
For Deshmukh & Rao, Advocates
